subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured cross-provider model fallback as consent to transfer user media, or add a separate provider media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: Current source shows real fallback media routing decisions, but changing the default or adding config affects privacy, compatibility, and fallback usefulness, which needs maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add a documented config/runtime policy that preserves compatibility by default while allowing users to restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document configured fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep current forwarding semantics and document that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text and media.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip media by default on cross-provider fallback and require an explicit opt-in for fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented config/runtime policy that preserves compatibility by default while allowing users to restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main-path work changed CLI fallback image replay and is closest to the current fallback media behavior.
